item.title: CVE-2026-91115 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. From 6.0.0 until 6.2.13, the writer option of i18nTextCollectorTask is passed to the dependency injector without validating that it names an allowed writer implementation. A crafted dev task URL can therefore instantiate arbitrary objects with attacker-controlled constructor arguments and execute code on the server. An administrator can be induced to run the task by following a link because the nested task did not require confirmation, and a site in dev mode exposes the path without authentication. CMS 5 is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

item.title: CVE-2026-97892 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.4
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.4 | LibreOffice checks the digital signatures of a PDF document when the document is opened, and shows whether each signature is valid. An out-of-bounds write existed when a signature was checked, because the parts of the file that a crafted signature claims to cover were not checked against the size of the file. In fixed versions a signature that claims to cover anything outside the file is reported as not valid.

item.title: CVE-2026-97894 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.4
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.4 | LibreOffice Calc can open spreadsheets in the DIF format, and text files such as CSV in the UTF-16 encoding. Both are read one line at a time. An out-of-bounds read existed when a line of a crafted file was read, because the length of the line could be miscalculated, so memory beyond the line could be copied into the imported document. In fixed versions each line is read up to its limit and no further.

item.title: CVE-2026-97999 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.4
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.4 | LibreOffice Base documents can hold an embedded HSQLDB database. When the experimental features option is enabled, LibreOffice offers to migrate such a database to the embedded Firebird engine when the document is opened. A heap buffer overflow existed when binary values were copied during the migration, because a value could be longer than the space set aside for its column. In fixed versions that space is enlarged whenever a value is longer than its column.

item.title: CVE-2026-98100 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.4
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.4 | LibreOffice can import documents in the HWP format, including pictures that link to an external file. An out-of-bounds read existed when the link target of a crafted picture was read, so memory past the picture data could end up in the converted document. In fixed versions the link target is taken only from the picture data.

item.title: CVE-2026-129295 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 4.2.0 until 4.6.1, attacker-controlled email headers can cause polynomial regular-expression backtracking during ordinary parse_from_string(), parse_from_bytes(), or parse_from_file() calls. In src/mailparser/utils.py, get_addresses() invokes the _ADDR_FALLBACK_RE fallback when strict address parsing yields no usable address, and overlapping quantifiers rescan padded address headers quadratically or cubically. In src/mailparser/const.py, parse_received() applies _CLAUSE_SPLITTER to uncollapsed whitespace in a Received header, causing quadratic backtracking when a whitespace run is not followed by a clause keyword. A small, well-formed message can keep mail gateway, ticketing, quarantine, or archival parsing workers busy for extended periods. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.1.

item.title: CVE-2026-129296 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 3.8.0 until 4.6.0, the write_attachments() and write_sample() APIs use attacker-controlled attachment filenames without sufficient sanitization and path containment validation. Directory traversal sequences and absolute filesystem paths can cause an attachment to be written outside the intended output directory. An attacker can overwrite files accessible to the parsing process when an application extracts attachments from a crafted message. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-129297 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. Prior to 4.6.2, get_server_ipaddress() can select an attacker-controlled address from attacker-controlled Received headers. The minimum mechanism needed to distinguish this spoofing issue, derived from the advisory's remediation analysis and verified fix evidence, is appearance-based candidate selection that can treat bracketed IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or HELO markers in sender-written text as MTA-recorded addresses and can continue past a trusted hop that names no address. Applications that rely on the returned value can attribute a message to an attacker-selected sender IP address. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.2.

item.title: CVE-2026-129299 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. Prior to 4.6.2, multiple message-processing behaviors can raise exceptions or silently lose content. Headers colliding with methods such as Parse, Message, and Write_Attachments can place bound method objects into parsed output and raise TypeError when a caller requests JSON serialization such as mail_json. When byte input is parsed through parse_from_bytes(), an 8-bit header value returned as email.header.Header can likewise raise TypeError when an X_raw accessor passes the value to json.dumps; both exceptions are outside the MailParserError hierarchy. Separately, rewritten names such as Subject_json and X_Spam_Flag can be substituted or disappear from mail, headers, and JSON output while has_defects remains false, and a headerless message can be treated as falsy before parser state is initialized, causing body and attachment properties to return empty values without an error signal. These behaviors can abort message processing or hide malicious indicators from downstream scanners. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.2.

item.title: CVE-2026-129300 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3 | mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 3.7.0 until 4.6.3, receiveds_format() in src/mailparser/utils.py catches only TypeError and ValueError while converting the trailing date of an attacker-controlled Received header. An out-of-range year can cause calendar.timegm() to raise OverflowError, and a sufficiently large timezone offset can cause datetime.fromtimestamp() to raise OSError. These exceptions are outside the MailParserError hierarchy, so one crafted header can abort the entire message parse through every parse_from_* entry point and may drop a queued batch. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.3.

item.title: CVE-2026-129301 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 4.6.0 until 4.6.3, write_attachments() calls _safe_attachment_filename() and write_sample() without isolating failures for individual attacker-controlled MIME parts. An RFC 2231 filename containing a NUL, a basename exceeding NAME_MAX, or an undecodable base64 payload can raise ValueError, OSError, or binascii.Error and abort the entire save loop. Later attachments remain unwritten; when a caller catches only MailParserError, the failure is not surfaced through the expected library-exception path. If a downstream scanner or sandbox reads only the extraction directory, a payload after the crafted part can be missed even though it remains in the delivered message, and the aborted batch also causes availability loss. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.3.

item.title: CVE-2026-129306 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.4
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.4 | libspdm is a sample implementation that follows the DMTF SPDM specifications. Prior to 3.8.3 and 4.0.0-rc2, libspdm_x509_verify_cert_chain() in os_stub/cryptlib_openssl/pk/x509.c and os_stub/cryptlib_mbedtls/pk/x509.c validates certificate signatures one link at a time instead of validating the complete X.509 path. In deployments using a pinned root with a constrained multi-tier PKI, an attacker holding a valid issuer credential below a constrained CA can present a subordinate certificate that exceeds pathLenConstraint or nameConstraints and may be accepted for SPDM identity validation. Exploitation requires the application to use libspdm's backend validation without an additional certificate-chain validation mechanism, the pinned root cannot be substituted, and the deployment's measurement policy must allow identity impersonation alone to satisfy its acceptance requirements. The mbedTLS backend remains unable to enforce nameConstraints because upstream mbedTLS does not implement that check. The full-chain validation changes are released in versions 3.8.3 and 4.0.0-rc2.

item.title: CVE-2026-119346 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.0
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.0 | Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 15.0.0 until 15.5.29 and 16.4.5, Next.js applications that use NextResponse to set cookies on Edge runtime routes expose the internal x-middleware-set-cookie header in the public response. This affects App Router route handlers and Pages Router Edge API routes. The header duplicates each cookie value and its attributes, so JavaScript already running on the same origin can read values that the Set-Cookie header marks HttpOnly, including sensitive session tokens set on an affected response. This issue is fixed in versions 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

item.title: CVE-2026-119348 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. Prior to 15.5.29 and 16.4.5, self-hosted Next.js App Router route handlers and the fetch cache that return a fetched upstream response unchanged can emit a response whose declared framing does not match the body actually sent. When the application is behind an HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy that permits pipelined response queueing, a crafted upstream response can desynchronize responses between clients. The resulting desynchronization can inject a response into another client's queue or disclose another client's response. This issue is fixed in versions 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

item.title: CVE-2026-119349 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.0.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js App Router applications that pass binary arguments, such as Uint8Array or Blob values, to functions using the 'use cache' directive can generate identical cache keys for distinct arguments. Requests with different binary arguments can therefore share a cached result, causing cross-user disclosure of cached data or allowing one request to poison results returned to another user. item.title: CVE-2026-119350 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.4.0 until 16.4.5, self-hosted Next.js applications served with next start can allow an unauthenticated request to poison a shared fallback shell when cacheComponents is true and partialPrefetching is unset or false. The affected dynamic route must have a prerenderable param declared by generateStaticParams whose requested value was not generated at build time, at least two never-prerenderable params below it, a layout that reads the shallower param inside a Suspense boundary, and a blocking fallback shell. A request-supplied placeholder route param whose path segment equals the percent-encoded bracketed name of its own deeper route param is incorrectly treated as unresolved, while the shallower concrete value is rendered into the shared shell and its HTTP status is persisted. Depending on application behavior, subsequent routes sharing that shell can receive a persistent 404 or attacker-selected substituted param text. Client hydration corrects substituted text, and the issue does not enable markup or script injection or disclose data. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

item.title: CVE-2026-119351 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.2.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications with Cache Components enabled can reuse an outer 'use cache' entry across root param values when a nested 'use cache' call reads a root param through next/root-params and returns a value containing pending promises. React Flight can deliver the ready portion to the outer function before the inner cache finishes publishing its root-param dependencies. The outer entry can then complete and be persisted under a key that omits the root param, causing the first written value to be served for other root param values and allowing the outer entry to ignore nested cache tag invalidation and lifetimes. The leaked value is not attacker controlled and depends on which invocation writes the entry first. This variant does not require an existing inner cache entry or a slow cache handler and is not covered by the fix for CVE-2026-103004. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

item.title: CVE-2026-119790 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.3 | Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.3.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications using the same 'use cache' function directly during rendering and through unstable_cache() can disclose cached data across root params when that function reads a root param. During the first fill after a cold process start, cross-request deduplication allows a concurrent unstable_cache() request to join the direct call's in-flight fill and receive its result before the root param mismatch is rejected. unstable_cache() then persists that result under a key that omits root params, causing later requests for other root param values to receive the same entry until revalidation or eviction. Exploitation requires the unstable_cache() request to arrive while the first fill is in flight. Outside this race, nesting 'use cache' inside unstable_cache() raises an unsupported-operation error, and avoiding that nesting prevents the issue. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

item.title: CVE-2026-129307 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3 | eml_parser serves as a python module for parsing eml files and returning various information found in the e-mail as well as computed information. In 3.0.3 and earlier, eml_parser.routing.parserouting() in eml_parser/routing.py builds a regular expression with multiple greedy capture groups and appends the npdate date literal extracted from a normalized copy of an attacker-controlled Received header, then searches that expression against the original unnormalized line. A formatting difference can make the trailing literal impossible to match, causing exhaustive backtracking across the greedy groups at each start position. The unsliced Received-header path is invoked by decode_email, decode_email_bytes, and parse_email, so one small unauthenticated message can pin a parser worker and create sustained queue backlog. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.4.

item.title: CVE-2026-83816 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1 | CodeWhale is a DeepSeek and MiMo coding agent for the terminal. Prior to 0.9.0, the ExecShellTool::approval_requirement_for path used is_parallel_readonly_command to downgrade commands to automatic approval based on a flag-stripped command allowlist. The allowlist treated fd, rg, and git grep as read-only even when fd -x or fd --exec, rg --pre, or git grep --open-files-in-pager selected an external program. registered_tool_approval_required returned without displaying a prompt for that automatic classification, and the later command-safety check also treated the base utilities as safe. Attacker-controlled content that influenced an agent tool call could therefore cause arbitrary program execution on the developer host without the approval promised by the default interactive profile, resulting in unauthorized access, modification, or disruption. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-83817 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | CodeWhale is a DeepSeek and MiMo coding agent for the terminal. Prior to 0.9.0, DEFAULT_AUTOMATION_AUTO_APPROVE caused AutomationRecord::task_auto_approve to resolve an omitted setting to true, and the automation_create schema advertised the same insecure default. enqueue_run_task converted that omission into an explicit true value, bypassing the safer task-path fallback and selecting ApprovalMode::Bypass for each scheduled run. After a user approved creation of an apparently benign recurring automation, subsequent executions could silently authorize mutating tools without a human present, and an automation created with shell access could repeatedly execute commands. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-87027 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.6
item.description: Monday 16 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.6 | In EDB Postgres Extended Server and EDB Postgres Advanced Server versions 15 through 18 with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled, the key used to encrypt temporary files was incompletely initialized. The code applied sizeof() to a pointer to the key buffer rather than to the buffer itself, so only 8 of the intended 32 bytes were filled from a secure random source and the remaining 24 bytes kept whatever was already in memory. This reduces the guaranteed randomness of the temporary-file key from 256 bits to 64 bits. Exploiting this requires local read access to the server's temporary-file directory, and those files normally exist only while the server is running; they persist only after a crash and are removed at the next server start. Permanent data files and WAL are not affected. The issue is fixed in EDB Postgres Extended Server 15.20, 16.16, 17.12 and 18.7 and EDB Postgres Advanced Server 15.20.0, 16.16.0, 17.12.0 and 18.7.0; the server must be restarted after upgrading.
